title: An unlisted structured Engram error code on admission falls to the Reconcile hold even when Engram reports it as transient
outcome: engram_admission_disposition (engram_queued_admission.rs:96-112 at be2ed177) maps every Degraded code outside ENGRAM_ADMISSION_RETRY_CODES to Reconcile, and so do structured remote codes passed through from the control reply (engram_host_adapter.rs:995). List Engram's transient codes, such as a busy or locked store or a temporary-unavailable code, and agree with Engram which of them are safe to re-admit automatically.
acceptance: A fail-first regression demonstrates that a producer-confirmed retry-safe transient structured admission/control code currently falls into a manual Reconcile hold instead of bounded automatic re-admission; the failed run and causal assertion are preserved.

A holder note records the current Engram producer codes and their admission/control phase semantics, with source locators and Engram-side concurrence on the exact classification: confirmed transient/retry-safe, definitive non-retryable, or semantically unknown. Unlisted or malformed codes default to a visible fail-closed hold; no text heuristic or guessed code authorizes retry.

For producer-confirmed transient failures where the retained attempt could not have begun, TermAl re-admits the same retained prompt using the shared bounded, durable, idempotent retry schedule and a fresh valid binding; tests show recovery without manual Resume, one delivery at most, exhaustion guidance, and restart recovery. Possibly-begun, authority-changed, non-retryable and unknown outcomes remain held without automatic delivery.
The full maintained five-stage gate passes on the exact committed input, and the note identifies the boundary with the existing retry-schedule and admission-retry changes.
